question: Does a same-root chronic cardiac pressure-overload experiment directly establish mature pathological fibrosis/dysfunction, then unload/retune, then re-impose the same pressure-overload challenge and show durable resistance across ECM, cell-state and function?
required_shape: direct mature pathological mechanical/fibrotic lock before retuning
delayed pressure unloading or other direct physical retuning
same or quantitatively equivalent adverse mechanical rechallenge
same-root comparison against naive challenged controls

cardiac_chronic_lock_roots.pre_retuning_state: LVH with dysfunction, myocyte enlargement and interstitial fibrosis
decompensated recoverable state at 4W and nonrecoverable state at 6W; collagen I alpha1 rises with progression
chronic pressure overload with LV dilation, functional decline and fibrotic-marker elevation
hypertrophy, interstitial fibrosis and impaired relaxation directly present at week 6
collagen volume fraction and myocardial stiffness measured before unloading

positive_rechallenge_control.evidence: repeat pressure overload produces attenuated hypertrophy/fibrosis and better function versus naive TAC 4W
positive_rechallenge_control.boundary: initial 3-day TAC does not establish mature fibrotic lock; therefore H3A must not be promoted to H3B

search_result.interpretation: A real literature gap is plausible, but absence from this search is not proof of nonexistence.

next_search.primary: citation-neighborhood and supplementary-method sweep around chronic 4W/6W/8W/10W TAC-deTAC roots for re-constriction/rebanding/reload cohorts
next_search.secondary: functional equivalents in joint capsule, tendon, vascular wall, valve and other mechanically fibrotic tissues
